title: After a fleet wave is stopped by a signal, `evolve loop --resume` resumes an unrelated stale checkpoint instead of the stopped lanes
summary: Wave 27 (1739, 1740) was stopped by SIGINT on the disk-full halt (2026-09-28). The loop printed "resume with: evolve loop --resume", but a signal stop in a fleet wave writes no checkpoint, so discovery (discoverPerRunResumeState: per-run cycle-state checkpoints with a resumable reason, newest first) found neither lane. It picked cycle 1709's quota checkpoint from 2026-09-27 and began building on that day-old base until it was stopped. The two lanes' claimed items could only be returned with `evolve inbox-mover recover-orphans`, which the message never named. A resumable checkpoint also never expires, however far main has moved.
fix: (1) A signal stop in a fleet wave either writes each unfinished lane's checkpoint (reason `signal`, resumable) or prints the true recovery: the lanes that stopped and `evolve inbox-mover recover-orphans` for their claims. It never names a resume that cannot continue them. (2) Resume refuses a checkpoint whose base is behind a later sealed cycle or older than a configured age, naming it and how to discard it (`evolve cycle reset`), instead of resuming it. (3) Discovery lists every live checkpoint it considered, so the operator sees the choice.
acceptance: After a SIGINT mid-wave, `evolve loop --resume` continues a stopped lane or refuses naming the lanes; it never picks an older unrelated checkpoint (red: it resumed 1709)
A checkpoint older than a later sealed cycle is refused with the reset command named
The stop message names the recovery that actually applies
